_source: CLAUDE.md §40 REAL-TIME CRITICAL PATH VS RESEARCH PATH. The ten stamps and the four percentiles below are §40's own lists, in §40's order and wording. scripts/tests/test_latency.py parses them back out of CLAUDE.md, so an eleventh stamp in the spec fails the build rather than going uninstrumented.
_reader: scripts/latency.py is the ONE recorder and the ONE summariser. A second place that times the order path would drift from this one, and two disagreeing latency numbers are worse than none.
_interval_semantics: §40 lists POINTS in time; a percentile needs an INTERVAL. Each stamp below is therefore recorded as the duration of the work that ENDS at that point -- `provider_receive` is the fetch, `normalization` is the normalisation, `decision_end` is the decision itself, `provider_acknowledgement` is the wait for the venue to answer. `decision_start` is the gap between the required analysis being ready and the decision beginning, which is the queueing latency §40 cares about and the only reading under which a start POINT has a duration at all.
_what_this_is_not: Not a performance budget. §40 does not set thresholds and neither does this file: it says latency must be MEASURED, and the repo's transport (REST polling and an MT5 file bridge) makes most absolute numbers a property of the poll interval rather than of the code. What the measurement is for is REGRESSION -- the same stage, the same machine, getting slower.
_percentiles_note: §40: 'Measure p50, p95, p99, max.' `max` is not a percentile and is reported separately, always with `n` (§39: always show sample size).

stamps.captured: the close time of the bar the decision reads (scripts/strategy-runner.py fetch_candles)
stamps._bound_why: This repo POLLS -- Binance REST klines and MT5 CSV exports. A bar's close time is the only event time available; the gap between it and our receipt is dominated by the poll interval, not by anything the code does. Recorded so the poll lag is visible and stops being invisible; not reported as an execution latency, because it is not one.

stamps.captured: when the candle fetch for a (symbol, timeframe) returns
after the rows are turned into the canonical candle shape and the §20 quality gate has run
after the derived analytics and the required methodology read for this tick (htf_context, the rule families)
entry to the per-signal §36 walk (scripts/decision_order.py Trace)

the per-signal §36 walk itself, recorded at BOTH of its exits -- the blocked signal that `continue`s and the eligible one that falls through to execution. Recorded at both rather than only the second, because a timer that stops only on the path that places an order measures the fast cases and drops the refusals, which are the slow ones.
§36 step 12-13: risk_precheck() and the sizing call inside it
when that venue call returns an order id
the venue's own fill time, read on the NEXT tick's reconcile
stamps._bound_why: A resting limit fills when the market reaches it, and this loop learns about it when it next polls. The span from submission to fill is therefore a market fact plus a poll interval, not a code latency. Recorded as a wall-clock fact on the trade, and deliberately NOT summarised into the same percentile table as the hot stages -- mixing them would make a slow tick indistinguishable from a patient limit order.

workloads._rule: CLAUDE.md §40: research, learning, backtesting, AI reasoning and post-trade analysis must NOT block the live decision and execution path. Isolation in this repo is BY PROCESS, and this table is what makes that claim checkable: every entry declares which path it belongs to and how it is kept off the other one.

research.isolated_by: a separate scanner process; the order path never waits on it (§35 classification decides what may gate)
scripts/build-artifact.py, run by the publish cron, never by the order loop
scripts/backtest-methods.py / stability-report.py, run by hand or by a research cron
not implemented (§41); when it arrives it belongs here
scripts/scan-loop.sh detaches every model read (`( nohup … & )`, stdin closed); the live path imports nothing that calls a model, and a repo-wide grep for anthropic/openai under scripts/ is empty
scripts/journal.py, detached from the order loop by scripts/pilot-loop.sh (2026-09-18: it used to run SYNCHRONOUSLY between the tick and the sleep)

_regression_note: §40's own list of what performance regression tests should cover. scripts/tests/test_latency.py asserts a benchmark exists for each, and that each runs offline -- a regression test that needs the network measures the network.
